name: Larp Builder - The Biblically Accurate North American Transit Experience
author: NoahGarrf
description:
This is an evil mod that adds the political, financial, and operational reality that North American transit agencies genuinely have to deal with.

These include:
    **Taxes:** You now draw sales taxes to help fund transit and pay for operating expenses. Rather than being reliant on operational profits, players will utilize tax income to pay for expansion and subsidize operations that do not turn a profit. Tax revenue is based off of sales taxes and calculates a maps actual population to calculate annual (daily) revenue!

**NIMBY resistance:**  Stations and tracks near existing buildings trigger community complaints with objections based on real concerns such as depth, elevation, property interactions, and even crime! Resolve them by paying for additional environmental reviews to placate the NIMBYs, redesigning stations to be deeper, or cancelling the station at that location all together.

**Realistic costs:** Construction, rolling stock, and maintenance are repriced to real world figures, with yearly inflation that compounds over the life of a save.

**Tax funding & elections:** Fund your agency through sales tax, raised by calling public votes that have have actual simulated elections based on expansion ambition and number of voters living near transit

**Federal grants and Ridership studies:** Apply for federal matching funds on large projects. Approval depends on a ridership study that can give an accurate prediction on your expansions ridership. Grants can be clawed back if actual ridership falls bellow a study's projections.

**Budget allocation:** Split tax revenue across policing, other transit divisions, and in-house delivery and deal with each of the real trade offs (crime reduction, pathfinding penalties, construction cost discounts).

**Crime, safety & faregates:** A dynamic crime rate influenced by policing spend and station gate upgrades, feeding back into pathfinding, elections, and grant approval.
